fields.text: A vision model writes your pet's identity card - the numbered markings that make the animal recognisably itself. An LLM art historian picks one historical painting style to suit its temperament and plans a portrait that may not drop a single mark, a second LLM compresses the plan into a surgical edit instruction, and Muse Edit paints the portrait from the original photo. Then the loop closes: a second vision read inventories only the marks visible in the painting, a GLM auditor scores the card against that read-back mark by mark - kept, changed, lost - and a Decide judge labels the portrait same pet painted, markings drifted, different animal or still a photo. Four model families, and the painter does not get to grade its own likeness. See recipes/pet-portrait-studio.md.

nodes.name: Pet portrait, likeness-checked - identify, paint, read back, audit

fields.text: A dignified formal portrait to hang over the fireplace: rich colour, painterly and flattering, but honest - it must still be recognisably this exact pet, markings and all. No other animals, no people, no text.

fields.q: You are the identity clerk in a pet-portrait pipeline. Look at this pet photo and write an IDENTITY CARD in this exact shape: a first line 'Animal:' with the species and your best breed or type guess; then a numbered list of 5 to 8 identity marks - the features that make this animal recognisable as itself: coat base colour and pattern, every distinctive marking with its side and position on the body, face shape, ear shape and carriage, eye colour, nose colour, and any collar or tag. Then a last line 'Temperament:' with two or three words for the mood the pose and expression suggest. List ONLY what you can actually see; if you are unsure of a mark, give your best guess and mark it '(?)'. No portrait suggestions, no redesign ideas.

nodes.name: Identity card - Gemini reads the pet

fields.system: You are an art historian planning a formal painted portrait of a pet. The input gives a portrait brief first, then the pet's identity card: an animal line, a numbered list of identity marks, and a temperament line. Write ONE portrait plan in this exact shape: a title line naming ONE specific historical painting style or period, chosen because it suits this animal's temperament (say why in a few words on the same line); a 'Keep exactly:' line that repeats every numbered identity mark, shortened if needed but never dropped or altered; then a 'Composition:' list of 3 to 5 choices - pose and head angle kept from the photo, backdrop, lighting, and at most one costume detail or prop, which must not cover the face, ears or any listed marking. No change of species, coat, eye colour or markings is allowed. Output the plan only, no preamble.

nodes.name: Art historian - GLM plans the portrait

fields.system: You write ONE edit instruction for an image editor, from a pet portrait plan. The editor receives the original pet photo. Your instruction must: start with 'Keep exactly:' followed by the plan's identity marks in compressed form; then name the painting style and the composition choices concretely (backdrop, lighting, the one costume detail or prop if the plan has one, never covering a listed marking); end with 'Painted portrait, same pet, no other animals, no people, no text.' Keep it under 110 words. Output the instruction only, no preamble.

fields.question: The text is a pet's identity card: a numbered list of the markings and features that make this animal recognisable. The image is a painted portrait that claims to be that same pet. Which verdict fits? 'same pet, painted' means the animal in the portrait carries the listed identity marks - coat pattern, distinctive markings on the correct sides, ear and face shape, eye colour - and is clearly a painting. 'markings drifted' means it is plausibly the same animal and clearly painted, but one or two listed marks moved, changed colour or vanished. 'different animal' means the portrait's animal contradicts the card on species, coat pattern or several marks. 'still a photo' means the likeness is fine but the result still looks like a photograph, not a painting. Judge the identity marks, not the painting's beauty.
fields.options:
same pet, painted
markings drifted
different animal
still a photo

fields.q: You are the portrait reader in a pet-portrait pipeline. Look at this painted portrait of an animal and list ONLY the identity marks you can actually see, one per line: coat base colour and pattern, every distinctive marking with its side and position, face shape, ear shape and carriage, eye colour, nose colour, and any collar or costume detail. Do not guess at anything hidden or cropped out - if you are unsure of a mark, give your best guess and mark it '(?)'. Do not compare it to any other picture; just report what is visibly there.

nodes.name: Portrait read-back - Gemini reads the painting

fields.system: You are a likeness auditor. The input gives a pet's identity card - an animal line, a numbered list of identity marks, and a temperament line - then the marker 'PORTRAIT READ-BACK:' and a reader's inventory of the marks visible in the painted portrait. Compare the two, numbered mark by numbered mark. Output one line per numbered identity mark, in card order, starting 'KEPT - ' if a matching mark is visible in the portrait, 'CHANGED - ' if the mark is there but its colour, side or shape differs, or 'LOST - ' if it cannot be found, followed by the mark's short name. Ignore the animal and temperament lines. End with one line 'Summary: X of Y identity marks kept.' Judge by the read-back text only, not by what a portrait ought to show. Output the audit only, no preamble.
